title: QBR: Customer Journey Stitch — Deck & Action Runbook
summary: Working draft of a modular QBR slide set plus a one-page action runbook that ties account health narratives to concrete renewal actions. Designed to let CSMs stitch together a customer journey story quickly for both standard (SMB/midmarket) and enterprise formats, with explicit play triggers and a compact renewal tracker schema.
purpose: Provide reusable, modular slide blocks and an operational runbook so a CSM can assemble a tailored QBR in under 45 minutes and leave with an ownerable renewal plan and sprint of follow-ups.
standard_deck_outline: Title + Meeting objectives (2 bullets: customer goals, expected outcomes)
Quick Wins & Adoption highlights (3–5 metrics or anecdotes)
Health Snapshot: Product usage, errors, support volume (1 slide; traffic-light scoring)
Value Realized: Top 3 success stories tied to business KPIs (customer quotes)
Gap & Opportunity heatmap: feature adoption vs suggested next steps (matrix)
Renewal posture & ask: suggested renewal options and timeline (be explicit)
Next 90-day plan: owners, milestones, success criteria (simple 3-line table)
Risks & Mitigations: top 3 risks and contingency playbacks
Wrap-up: decisions needed, commitment, next check-in date
enterprise_deck_outline: Executive snapshot: TL;DR value, ARR at risk/opportunity, exec sponsor alignment
Strategic alignment: how our roadmap maps to their initiatives (2–3 bullets)
Adoption deep-dive: active seats, workflows instrumented, latency/cost anecdotes
Quality/regression review: recent incidents, RCA status, SLA adherence
Total Cost of Ownership: cost-per-unit token, optimization recommendations
Risk scoring and escalation path: how we will engage support/engineering
Contract levers & commercial options: tiering, dedicated capacity, migration offers
Governance asks: compliance items, audit timeline, SSO/KMS checkpoints
Program plan: cross-functional owners (CS, AE, Eng, Solutions), milestones, gating criteria
Decision log and signatures: who signs for renewal, procurement notes
renewal_runbook_steps: Prep (14–21 days): pull metrics dashboard, sales contract summary, last 3 support tickets; update slide blocks
Risk triage (10 days): classify as low/medium/high; if high, trigger enterprise escalation and schedule pre-brief with AE
Pre-brief (7 days): 20-minute internal sync — confirm ask and roles; lock slide deck
Customer QBR (0): present tailored deck; capture decisions in decision log; agree next steps with owners and dates
Post-QBR (1–3 days): send recap + recording + agreed action list; update renewal tracker
Sprint (3–30 days): sprint of actions owned by cross-functional team; weekly short updates; escalate blockers
Commercial close (30–90 days): finalize proposal, legal loop, procurement checklist; confirm signature and update tracker
meeting_script_snippets: Open: 'Today’s objective is to confirm the outcomes we delivered and align on the 90-day plan that supports your Q4 objective of X.'
Value recap: 'In the last 90 days, you saw a Y% drop in latency and Z% improvement in throughput — here’s what that enabled.'
Handling objection: 'I hear concerns about cost — here are two optimisation levers we can activate immediately and one longer-term commitment.'
Closing ask: 'Assuming these actions look good, are you comfortable we move forward with the renewal timeline we discussed?'
risk_signals_and_triggers: Delayed procurement steps (PO not submitted within 30 days of proposal)
Repeated feature regressions impacting critical flows
suggested_metrics_and_sources: Tokens/embeddings per feature — usage DB / billing export
Adoption by team/department — custom adoption table (spreadsheet)
visual_assets_tips: Use a one-line customer quote on the value slide (real quote + initials)
Heatmap: grayscale cells with red/amber/green overlays for quick scanning
Include a compact roadmap snippet when discussing long-term commitments
Embed 30-second demo GIFs for adoption highlights (host externally and link)
For enterprise decks, include org chart visual with named sponsors and procurement contacts
notes_to_self: This doc is intentionally modular — duplicate slide blocks and swap metrics depending on audience
Avoid overloading slides: 3 bullets max per slide for exec-facing portions
Test deck populate script (not yet implemented) to pull metrics from billing and telemetry
